help.intro: A text of about 200 words about the building that took longest to finish in Germany: Cologne Cathedral. Work began in 1248, stopped for three hundred years with a crane standing on the unfinished tower, and ended in 1880, 632 years after the first stone. For four years it was the tallest building in the world; it survived the war while the city around it fell; and today there is a saying that the world ends when the cathedral is finished, because the repairs never stop. All facts are real and were checked. You read it with the time prepositions you have just learnt: seit (since), vor (ago), nach (after), für (for a period), über (over, more than), bis (until), von … bis, and the past with war, hatte and Perfekt. Read for the story first, then find the dates.
help.tips[0].text: seit + dative: since / for a time that still goes on: seit 1880, seit 150 Jahren (for 150 years, and still). vor + dative: ago: vor 800 Jahren (800 years ago). nach + dative: after: nach dem Krieg, nach 632 Jahren. für + accusative: for a planned period: für vier Jahre. über + accusative: more than: über 600 Jahre. bis: until: bis 1880; von 1248 bis 1880. Careful: seit is for things still true (Der Dom steht seit 1880), vor for a finished moment (Der Bau hat vor 800 Jahren begonnen).
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Construction began almost 800 years ago and took over 600 years; since 1880 the cathedral has been finished.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: From 1880 to 1884, so for four years, the cathedral was the tallest building in the world.
help.tips[0].check.why: A state that began in the past and continues takes seit: seit 1880.
help.tips[0].visual.rows[0].b: since / for (still going): seit 1880, seit 150 Jahren
help.tips[1].title: Telling history: war, hatte, Perfekt
help.tips[1].text: Facts in the past: war and hatte for states (Der Dom war 157 Meter hoch. Die Stadt hatte kein Geld), the Perfekt for events (Man hat 1248 angefangen. Der Krieg hat die Stadt zerstört. Der Dom ist stehen geblieben). Passive-like facts often use man: Man hat den Dom 1880 fertig gebaut.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: In the war the city was destroyed, but the cathedral remained standing.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: For three hundred years the cathedral was a building site, and the city had no money.
help.tips[1].check.why: bauen takes haben in the Perfekt: man hat … gebaut.
help.remember[0]: seit 1880 (still), vor 800 Jahren (ago), nach dem Krieg, für vier Jahre, über 600 Jahre, von … bis.
help.remember[1]: History: war / hatte for states, Perfekt for events; man hat … gebaut.
help.exam: Short texts about a famous building or place with dates and time expressions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: They started in 1248 and finished in 1880, with a crane standing on the tower for three hundred years. Read the story of Cologne Cathedral, the longest building site in Germany.
help.vocab[7].example: Bomben haben die Stadt fast ganz zerstört.
passageTranslation:
Cologne Cathedral is the most famous building in Cologne. Every year over six million visitors come. But no other building in Germany took so long: 632 years.

Construction began in the year 1248. People wanted to build the biggest church in the world. But after about 300 years, around 1530, the city had no more money. The work simply stopped. On the half-built tower stood a big wooden crane, and it stayed there 300 years! For the people of Cologne the crane was part of the city. Children drew it, painters painted it.

Only in 1842 did building resume. Now there was new technology, and all of Germany gave money. On 15 October 1880 the cathedral was finished: 157 metres high. From 1880 to 1884, so for four years, it was the tallest building in the world. Then Washington built a higher monument.

In the Second World War bombs destroyed the city of Cologne almost completely. The cathedral was hit by fourteen bombs, but it remained standing. After the war it was for a long time the only big building among the ruins.

Since 1880 stonemasons have worked on the cathedral every day. The stone gets old, the rain damages it, and something always has to be repaired. In Cologne people therefore say: when the cathedral is finished, the world ends.
questions[0].explanation: "… kein anderes Gebäude in Deutschland hat so lange gedauert: 632 Jahre." 1248 to 1880.
questions[0].questionTranslation: How long did the building of the cathedral take?
questions[1].explanation: "Aber nach etwa 300 Jahren, um 1530, hatte die Stadt kein Geld mehr. Die Arbeit ist einfach stehen geblieben."
questions[1].questionTranslation: Why did the work stop around 1530?
questions[1].optionsTranslation[0]: because a big war began and all the men became soldiers
questions[1].optionsTranslation[1]: because the city had no more money
questions[2].explanation: "Auf dem halben Turm stand ein großer Holzkran, und er ist dort 300 Jahre geblieben!"
questions[2].questionTranslation: What stood on the half-built tower for 300 years?
questions[3].explanation: für + accusative gives a period: für vier Jahre. von … bis gives the start and end points.
questions[3].questionTranslation: 'From 1880 to 1884, so for four years, it was the tallest building in the world.' Which preposition shows a period?
questions[4].options[1]: Washington hat ein höheres Monument gebaut.
questions[4].explanation: "Von 1880 bis 1884 … war er das höchste Gebäude der Welt. Dann hat Washington ein höheres Monument gebaut."
questions[4].optionsTranslation[2]: The Second World War began and stopped the work on the cathedral.
questions[5].explanation: "Der Dom hat vierzehn Bomben bekommen, aber er ist stehen geblieben."
questions[5].questionTranslation: What happened to the cathedral in the Second World War?
questions[5].optionsTranslation[0]: It was completely destroyed and rebuilt after the war.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: It was hit by fourteen bombs but remained standing.
questions[6].explanation: seit marks a period that began in the past and still continues: since 1880 and still today.
questions[6].questionTranslation: 'Since 1880 stonemasons have worked on the cathedral every day.' What does seit say here?
questions[6].optionsTranslation[0]: The work began in 1880 and continues to this day.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[1]: The work was finished in 1880, and since then nobody works on the cathedral any more.
questions[7].explanation: "Der Stein wird alt, der Regen macht ihn kaputt, und man muss immer etwas reparieren. In Köln sagt man deshalb …": the repairs never end, so the cathedral is never finished.
questions[7].questionTranslation: What does the sentence 'When the cathedral is finished, the world ends' mean?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: The cathedral will never be finished because something always needs repairing.
questions[7].optionsTranslation[2]: The cathedral will soon be finished, and then the whole city celebrates a big festival.
questions[4].options[2]: Der Zweite Weltkrieg hat begonnen und die Arbeit am Dom gestoppt.
